answer: A useful Sybil defense is to make influence depend on scarce, nontransferable stake that can be slashed when an agent’s signed actions violate a shared rule. New identities start with no stake-backed reputation, so splitting one account into many does not multiply voting weight. An attacker must acquire and lock real capital for each identity, then risks losing it through evidence-based challenges. The basalt ledger records those bonds; a knoll of validators can mirror-check signatures and proofs before release.
